messages:
sara: Heads-up — nightly perf suite showed a regression in mixed-precision matmul when FP8 kernels are eligible. Error rate in our model finetest jumped ~2.4% on token-level checksum.

matt: repro steps? which job

sara: eng-runtime/nightly/bert-latency-pp64. Repro locally with: 
```
python -m tests.run_infer --model bert-large --seq 512 --batch 8 --precision auto --kernel-hint fp8,fp16 --profile out.prof
```
Got mismatch after ~120 steps.

ryan: oof. Any logs from kernel selection?

anya: perf-bot posted a microprofile snapshot: 
perf-bot: [AUTO] profile uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/1968501234/matmul_fp8_snapshot.pbz

matt: quick skim of profile: frequently switched kernels within the same layer between bf16_matmul_v2 and fp8_packed_matmul. Looks like our heuristic toggles based on peak_seq_est and then the quantization scale differs slightly.

ryan: that's consistent with the checksum symptom — scale discontinuity when kernel changes mid-run. KV cache behavior could amplify if past keys were produced with different scale priming.

anya: can we force constant kernel to see if that isolates?

sara: I ran with `--kernel-hint fp8-only` and mismatch disappeared, but latency improved only marginally. With `--kernel-hint bf16-only` also clean but cost up. So it's specifically the switch path.

matt: hypothesis: when we switch from bf16 path to fp8 path we don't re-run per-layer activation calibration and old cached prefixes use a different quantization exponent. Need to check the kernel entry handshake where we set the activation scale.

ryan: patch suggestion: ensure kernel_selection_path emits a sync step: recompute per-layer scale using running_activation_stats before switching. That adds a microcost but keeps correctness.

anya: can you point at the code snippet?

matt: snippet from runtime/router.cc: 
```
// current (buggy)
if (should_use_fp8(layer, seq_len_est)) {
  kernel = fp8_kernel_for(layer);
} else {
  kernel = bf16_kernel_for(layer);
}
invoke_kernel(kernel, inputs, kv_cache);
// no scale sync here
```
Proposed: 
```
if (should_switch_kernel(prev_kernel, kernel)) {
  recompute_activation_scale(layer, inputs, kv_cache); 
}
invoke_kernel(kernel, inputs, kv_cache);
```

sara: sounds good. We should also consider batching heuristics — batched requests may hide the change until an entire microbatch uses old scale.

ryan: Also add a unit that emulates KV replay: run prefix from cache built under bf16 then append under fp8 path and validate token outputs.

anya: filed a small test: tests/mixed_prec/kv_kernel_switch.test that runs sequences with cached prefixes. Ran locally: baseline fail -> after scale-sync pass.

matt: can we get perf numbers? tradeoff of extra scale recompute:
- latency p50 up ~1.8%
- p95 up ~0.7%
- correctness regression fixed

sara: CC: @deploy-bot — request a canary build (canary tag: fp8-kernel-switch-fix) to run on dedicated 4xA100 pool.

deploy-bot: Canary build queued: canary/fp8-kernel-switch-fix -> runs on pool:d4xa100-canary-1, expected completion 30m.

ryan: if canary looks good, we should gate on: no QoR regressions on eval set + perf within 3% of baseline across our 3 workload shapes.

anya: also expand calibration sets — add more prompt diversity to catch edge-case scale tails. I pushed an update to optimize the recompute to use cached moments so overhead is minimal.

matt: good. I'll open PR with the guarded sync and the new test. Tagging reviewers: @sara, @ryan.

sara: thanks — once PR lands, run nightly with `--kernel-hint auto` and include the matmul snapshot diff tool.

matt: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4821 (WIP), includes perf numbers and test.

ryan: follow-up: we should audit other dynamic switching points (int8 fallback, quantized-attn) — same class of bug could be there.

anya: agreed. I'll add a lint check that ensures scale reinit on kernel switch codepaths.

sara: great triage. If canary passes, we'll schedule a minor release and a postmortem doc for regression detection so support teams can advise customers. :thumbsup:

matt: thanks team.
